clue.text: Got a loan outside bank, interest-free?

indicators.note: one word sits outside the other, wrapping round it

parts.note: someone bored has no interest left
a bank of seats or keys is a row of them

explanation.surface: Someone took out a loan away from the bank, with no interest charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest-free' looks like loan terms, but it describes someone with no interest in anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To have borrowed is to have received something as a loan, past tense matching 'Got'.

clue.text: Caught learner initially exiting big intersection on other side

indicators.note: letters that are exiting leave the longer word behind

parts.note: a cloverleaf is a large road junction with looping slip roads
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the opening letter of learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A driver is caught out, with a learner leaving a huge road junction on the far side.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C and L from CLOVERLEAF and OVERLEAF remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Overleaf means printed on the reverse of the page, i.e. on the other side of the sheet.

clue.text: Specialized corps in army role, as arranged

indicators.note: things arranged are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: An elite unit is given a special part within the army, as planned.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Marines are Britain's naval infantry, a commando force distinct from the army.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Marines are a specialist amphibious commando force, a corps in its own right.

clue.text: Not beyond showing humour with short clue

indicators.note: short means cut down, losing the final letter

explanation.surface: A setter shows humour while keeping a clue brief, within limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Within is the opposite of beyond, meaning inside the limits.

clue.text: Early deposits, we hear, in regular payment

definitions.note: the answer is plural, the definition singular in form

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken word, matched by its sound alone

parts.note: dew is moisture deposited early in the morning

explanation.surface: Money paid in early makes up a regular instalment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposits' looks like banking, but these are the morning drops of dew.
explanation.definitionFit: Dues are fees paid regularly, such as club membership subscriptions.

clue.text: Dangerous striker in the box, one grabbed by Scottish player

indicators.note: what is grabbed is held inside the grabber's grip

parts.note: the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: A striker in the penalty box, the danger man, is grabbed by a Scottish footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface hides a snake; 'the box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit viper is a venomous snake, and snakes strike at their prey.

clue.text: Funding a grand opera? Doesn't sound like it!

parts.note: surface padding: a wry aside that the opera is not pronounced like the two pieces

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether money is going to a big opera production, then says it doesn't seem so.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail admits that the opera's name is not pronounced like 'aid a': it is said eye-EE-da.
explanation.definitionFit: Aida is Verdi's grand opera set in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Watching big game, top journalist described what happened in court

parts.note: watching a match means being at it
a Test is a full international cricket match

explanation.surface: A senior journalist at a major match reports the events on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests tennis but means a court of law, where witnesses give evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness formally, so a witness attested in court to the events.

clue.text: Of a political type different to us, in NI?

indicators.note: letters made different are rearranged into another order

parts.note: taken as written; NI is Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Asks whether a political persuasion in Northern Ireland differs from ours.
explanation.walkthrough: Unionists in Northern Ireland favour staying in the United Kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Unionist describes politics supporting union with Britain, a political type especially in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Brave — ultimately afraid, see, of nobody

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Being brave means that in the end you fear no one.
explanation.definitionFit: To brave something is to face it boldly, the verb sense of defying it.

clue.text: Man's covered by notice I check and copy — stick with it

indicators.note: being covered by something here means coming just after it in the line

explanation.surface: A man is included in a notice that I check and duplicate, so stick with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesive tape is what you stick things with, a sticky strip; the definition is descriptive.

clue.text: Rogue, leader of thieves, Russian forger?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a rouble is the Russian currency, so someone making them illicitly

explanation.surface: A villain heads a gang of thieves, perhaps a Russian counterfeiter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical 'rouble maker'.
explanation.definitionFit: A troublemaker is a mischievous person who stirs up strife, which a rogue does.

clue.text: Malinger, albeit poorly in earliest stage

indicators.note: something done poorly is botched, so the letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone shirks while poorly, even if only in the early stages of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Germinal means relating to a germ or seed, so at the very beginning of development.

clue.text: Cautiously move below large rocky ridge

indicators.note: in a down entry, below means placed underneath the next item

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
to edge is to move slowly and carefully

explanation.surface: A climber inches beneath a big rocky outcrop.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow shelf of rock projecting from a cliff face.

clue.text: Reminder for actor in carefree play, in part

indicators.note: in means put inside the following item

parts.note: PT is the abbreviation for part
a romp is boisterous, lighthearted play

explanation.surface: An actor in a lighthearted show gets a nudge about part of his lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' and 'part' suggest theatre, but they only give ROMP and PT.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt is a word fed to an actor who has forgotten a line.

clue.text: Service area set back a long way away

indicators.note: set back means turned to run in the opposite direction

parts.note: the Royal Air Force, one of the armed services
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A military base area has been relocated far off.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar is a literary adverb for at or from a great distance.

clue.text: Meeting, with skill, covering disorder up

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round the other part
in a down entry, up means read from the bottom to the top

explanation.surface: A meeting is run skilfully, hiding the chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly is a gathering of people for a common purpose, such as a school meeting.

clue.text: Stranger not even seen by monarch

explanation.surface: An unknown person is not even granted an audience with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun, but it is the comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Odder is the comparative of odd, meaning more peculiar or unusual.

clue.text: Remote lake Stanley finally found in expedition

indicators.note: things found in something sit inside it

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Evokes the explorer Stanley discovering a distant lake on an African expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: L and Y go inside OUTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlying means far from the centre, distant or remote.

clue.text: Offer to wrap new tie

indicators.note: wrapping something puts it inside the wrapper

explanation.surface: Someone offers to gift-wrap a new necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie' looks like a gift, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind is to tie or fasten together with cord.

clue.text: Somebody else supported by a line? Only in theory

parts.note: what rests on something is supported by it
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone else's backing of a policy line holds only on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Notional means existing as an idea rather than in reality, hypothetical.

clue.text: Something played in time by title-holder?

parts.note: a book's spine carries its title
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A champion plays something in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title-holder' suggests a champion but is the back of a book; T goes next to SPINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord, an instrument that is played.

clue.text: Request access to have meal inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within the other word

parts.note: eats is a colloquial word for food; to eat is to have a meal

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be let in to get something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea, a request made with urgency.

clue.text: Deliberately lost, like defeated wrestler, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a match fixed by losing on purpose
second meaning: hurled to the mat

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses suggest a rigged bout, but they are independent.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrown contest is lost intentionally, and a wrestler thrown by an opponent has been floored.

clue.text: Male lawyer of bad repute in East producing general panic

indicators.note: in means placed within the following place

parts.note: a shyster is an unscrupulous lawyer

explanation.surface: A disreputable male lawyer in the Far East whips up widespread alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion splits the region's name after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass hysteria is collective panic spreading through a population.

clue.text: Small object put in post

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: A little item is dropped into the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: To send is to dispatch, as by putting something in the post.

clue.text: Theorem regularly selected for school period

indicators.note: regularly selected means taking every other letter at even intervals

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A theorem is routinely chosen for study during a school session.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is one of the divisions of the school year.

clue.text: Part of Southern England understood in North

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the south-eastern English county
second meaning: Scots and northern English for known

explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland and northern England, ken means to know, with its past form spelt with a T ending.
explanation.definitionFit: The county is in south-east England, and the dialect past participle of ken means known or understood.

clue.text: Put in solitary, fellow citizen of ours

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: a loner is a solitary person
to don is to put on clothes

explanation.surface: One of our own citizens has been placed in solitary confinement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Telegraph is a London paper, so 'of ours' points to its home city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Londoner is an inhabitant of London, the newspaper's own city.

clue.text: Primate, in practice, preceded by bishop, say

indicators.note: preceded by means another item comes before this one

parts.note: a bishop is a chess man

explanation.surface: An archbishop, practising, follows a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: A primate is also a church's senior archbishop, which the bishop plays on; here it is the monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandrill is a large West African baboon with a colourful face, a primate.
